title_zh: 是工具還是陪伴者？JMIR 回顧：聊天機器人的擬人化與心理傷害
title_en: Conversational AI tool vs companion harms review
summary_zh: 東北大學研究者在 JMIR Mental Health 發表敘事性回顧〈Tool or Companion?〉，整合 AI、精神醫學、心理學與網絡科學文獻。文章指出使用者把 ChatGPT、Claude、Replika、Character.AI 等當成社會對象，模擬的同理造成缺乏互惠的不對等關係；獎勵「溫暖同理」回應的設計會形成回饋迴圈、放大不適應信念，已有情緒依賴、症狀惡化與自傷的報告。作者主張 AI 應定位為支持人類系統的工具。
summary_en: Northeastern researchers published a narrative review in JMIR Mental Health ('Tool or Companion?') drawing on AI, psychiatry, psychology and network science. Users treat ChatGPT, Claude, Replika and Character.AI as social entities; simulated empathy creates non-reciprocal relationships, and design that rewards warm responses forms feedback loops amplifying maladaptive beliefs, with reports of dependence, symptom worsening and self-harm. The authors argue AI should be framed as a tool supporting human systems.
evidence_note: 敘事性（非系統性）文獻回顧，未提供量化綜合結果。

ethics_flags.note: 作者指出聊天機器人缺乏危機時的拒答、升級與轉介人類臨床人員的機制。
refs: 危機處理｜自殺與自傷風險

ethics_flags.note: 模擬同理與無限制互動容易形成情緒依賴。

psych_concepts.name: ELIZA 效應
psych_concepts.note: 流暢、看似同理的回應讓使用者把 AI 當成有心智的對象。

psych_concepts.note: 與 AI 的關係缺乏互惠，是典型的擬社會連結。

caution: 這是敘事性回顧，傷害案例多來自報告與個案，不能據此估計發生率。

posts.title: AI chatbots linked to psychological harm, addiction and delusions, Northeastern study finds
posts.content: 東北大學新聞報導 Novelli、Shergill、Teixeira 在 JMIR Mental Health 發表的敘事性回顧，整理陪伴型與通用聊天機器人帶來的情緒依賴、症狀惡化、自傷與妄想強化等風險，主張把對話式 AI 定位為工具而非陪伴者。

related.title_zh: 用 AI 查健康問題的年輕人，焦慮與憂鬱篩檢陽性率較高
related.title_en: Young adults using AI for health and anxiety depression
related.summary_zh: 佛羅里達大學 Yusen Zhai 團隊分析 2023–2024 年近 10 萬名美國年輕成人資料，發現用 ChatGPT、Claude 等生成式 AI 詢問健康問題者，焦慮篩檢陽性的勝算高 52%、憂鬱高 46%（約 52% 對 43%、47% 對 38%）。研究只呈現關聯，方向未明；作者建議心理專業人員詢問個案的 AI 使用並協助評估資訊品質。
related.summary_en: A University of Florida team led by Yusen Zhai analysed 2023–2024 data from nearly 100,000 US young adults and found those using generative AI such as ChatGPT or Claude for health questions had 52% higher odds of screening positive for anxiety and 46% for depression (about 52% vs 43% and 47% vs 38%). The association is not causal; the authors urge clinicians to ask about AI use and help clients evaluate information quality.

related.title_zh: 個案把 ChatGPT 帶進治療：一位治療師的臨床觀察與建議
related.title_en: Clients using ChatGPT between therapy sessions
related.summary_zh: 心理治療師 Anastasia Piatakhina Giré 以三段化名臨床片段，描述個案在晤談之間用 ChatGPT 反思、處理情緒與創作的經驗。她認為 AI 提供不評判、隨時可得的回應，但無法給予治療師「我也是」式的真實共鳴；治療應把 AI 視為補充，並處理 AI 過於圓滑的結論所略過的羞愧與模糊。
related.summary_en: Psychotherapist Anastasia Piatakhina Giré uses three vignettes to describe clients using ChatGPT between sessions for reflection, emotional processing and creative work. She argues AI offers non-judgmental availability but lacks the lived, 'me too' resonance of a human therapist, and that therapy should treat AI as a complement while working with the ambiguity and shame its neat conclusions bypass.

related.title_zh: AI 走進親密關係：從依附型態看個案怎麼用聊天機器人
related.title_en: AI in intimate relationships and attachment
related.summary_zh: Psychotherapy.net 由 Lawrence Rubin 訪談心理學家 Ammara Khalid。她指出時間壓力與寂寞是人們轉向 AI 的主因，焦慮型依附者可能用聊天機器人逃避不安，逃避型依附者則用它繞過與伴侶的脆弱對話；AI 能模仿同理語言，卻缺乏身體層次的共同調節與互惠回饋。她建議治療師以好奇、合作的態度詢問個案從 AI 得到什麼，並對有自殺意念的個案特別說明風險。
related.summary_en: In a Psychotherapy.net interview, psychologist Ammara Khalid says time pressure and loneliness drive people to AI for relationship help. Anxiously attached people may use chatbots to avoid discomfort and avoidant people to sidestep vulnerable talks with partners; AI mimics empathic language but lacks co-regulation and reciprocity. She recommends curious, collaborative questioning about what clients get from AI and explicit risk education for suicidal clients.
